newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Inespal strike seen making little impact.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Inespal strike seen making little impact.

text.p: Spanish state holding company SEPI, owner of aluminium producer Inespal, said on Friday the impact of a series of strikes was likely to be very minimal.
A SEPI spokesman said final figures for Thursday's 24-hour strike attendance were not available, but production was unlikely to have been greatly affected.
"This is the kind of output which requires minimum services to be guaranteed. So the impact will be minimum, anyway, no matter what the strike attendance," the spokesman said.
Workers were striking in protest at goverment plans to privatise the firm.
He reiterated that talks with Aluminum Company of America (Alcoa) for the sale of Inespal were continuing.
"Alcoa has presented its industrial plan, which was considered as one of the most important conditions (for the sale)," he said.
Alcoa's plan, which was presented to trade unions, did not foresee any staff reductions, he said.
Before talks continue, matters such as the value of the offer needed to be settled.
Last February, Alcoa and SEPI signed a preliminary agreement for Alcoa to buy Inespal's main businesses by end-1997.
